spiritual_reading:
The disorder that burst forth from governing falsities and evils as a gross external principle rose up against the revealed pattern of Divine mediation. It was rejected from higher ordered states and was driven down into the lowest degree, because those higher states would not admit it into their harmonies. When it entered the lowest level of life it organized itself into a fixed system of perverted perception, established itself in that system, and brought forth works from it. And when those malformed works again fell into the lowest level, the same disorder returned in them.

In those works it took on their quality and spoke through the chief ruling falsity. That leading falsity said to its allied falsities: Unite your understanding with mine, and I will fabricate for you a human likeness modeled on the loftier pattern. What it proposed, they carried out: they yielded their borrowed insight, and from it the imitation was produced.

That disordering principle—this gross external influence that had perceived the Divine pattern, had organized a perverted system, and had lodged within it—afterwards rose again within the resulting works. From there it entered into the governing falsities and evils, and by its driving force they produced a new human appearance, both an internal and an external, modeled on the loftier pattern. Through the efficacy of that disorder which had perceived the Divine pattern, it passed into the governing powers by means of those works; it took them over, and they too brought forth successive states from themselves, each according to its ruling inclination—one state preserving some likeness to the true form, another losing it.

Consider this teaching: the lower governing powers shaped the first internal and external human state by the activity of that disorder which entered them by means of works; thus a human form was established according to the loftier pattern.

The formative power then arranged within that human form faculties for receiving and acting, both outwardly and inwardly, and distributed them into ordered regions. For everything that these faculties and their elemental operations take in from the outermost life, there are inward retentive capacities and ordered recesses, so that what is received can be preserved. Whenever inquiry is made for what has been deposited within those inward retentions, the faculty brings forth what it has taken in and supplies it to the one who seeks it.

In this way the outward capacity for discernment is provided with an ordered ability to notice every kind of quality presented to it in the outermost life.

Likewise the faculty of outward understanding has ordered retentive capacities within it, so that every appearance it takes in—whether aligned with good or with evil, whether it excites love or aversion or craving—can be received and held within inward memory. And whenever that outward understanding chooses to bring forward what it took in, it can enter its inward retentions at will, reflect, search, and draw out what was stored, and present it to the inquirer who requested it—whether it be what serves craving, or what serves genuine love, or what serves aversion; and thus that faculty produces and does what belongs to each kind of reception.

The faculty of receptivity to instruction also has inward retentive capacities. Whatever it takes in—whether aligned with good or with evil—is received and placed within its inner memories, and is preserved there even through long duration. After long duration, if inquiry is made for what it took in at some time and preserved, it immediately enters its inner memories, searches, reviews, and retrieves that particular teaching, and brings it out from the state in which it was first stored.

In like manner the faculty that discerns subtle quality functions in the same way as outward understanding and receptivity to instruction: whatever quality it perceives it takes in and deposits within inward memory. Whenever it is questioned, it returns to those memories and recalls what it has retained.

Further, the faculty that discerns appropriations and delights has an inner power dwelling in it. This faculty too has distinct retentive capacities. It receives such appropriations, gathers them, and at any time inquiry is made about a particular delight it can send it forth and recall it, even supplying the distinctive sign of that delight, and thus giving its remembered quality to whoever asks.

Again, the faculty of direct contact with outermost things is similar: when it makes contact, it receives the memory of that contact and stores it inwardly until inquiry is made for it; then it returns to its inner memory, draws out what it retained from that contact, and gives it to whoever asks.

And the central governing faculty that presides over all of them is most fully of this pattern: everything that these five outward faculties receive and lay up for that central faculty, it receives and guards. Whenever their deposit is requested, it sends out and returns everything that was entrusted to it.

For the deliberation of that central faculty is as a ruling authority: with it are the subordinate reasonings of its community and the directive powers of its active life. Whenever these subordinate powers ask for what they desire, it supplies the judgment and counsel by which they proceed.

Moreover, it is as an inward steward: whatever is entrusted to it, it receives and arranges distinctly in ordered forms and distinct places, and it can produce it again from the very state in which it was placed.

So too the faculty that coordinates outer action operates in this way. Whatever discernment presents to it and it receives, it can bring forth again from the inward retentions where it stored it, and supply it whenever it is called for.

Likewise whatever receptivity to instruction presents to it and it receives: whenever it is asked for that teaching, it produces and gives what was heard to whoever asks.

And the remaining outward faculties follow the same order; whenever their stored contents are requested, they can be brought forth and given.

Yet protections are stationed at these entrances, and restraints are fixed there under the control of those protections.

It is like the order by which a community guards its approaches with vigilant oversight and fixed checkpoints: the inner holding states are behind, and restraints are set upon the entrances; the guards govern those restraints while they stand at the point of admission. Thus what is native to that community’s life and agrees with its ruling love is admitted by their consent; but what is foreign to its ruling love is resisted and held back, not being allowed to enter. And another thing may be admitted only with great difficulty before it is received. Within are many inner containments and many controlling restraints; and when the directive power chooses, it handles the restraints, opens admission, and draws out what had been hidden within.

So the whole outward life is like a powerful organized domain, and its admissions and their guards are like the outermost access points of the human life. These admissions are the ways by which discernment, instruction, and subtle discrimination take in influences, and also the ways by which the life expresses what it has formed. Many sentinels and a multitude of guards are set over the outer faculties, protecting their admissions. And the directing faculty within is the commander of that whole domain, so that whenever it wills it can open, and whenever it wills it can shut.

But when higher understanding enlightened by Divine truth approaches to enter the outer admissions of life, the governing falsities and evils that serve as gatekeepers hinder and restrain it. They bind the whole outer circuit of life so that what they treat as alien cannot enter.

Nevertheless, enlightened understanding by its wisdom, reverence, and persistent effort humbles those guards set over the outer admissions. When it has finished humbling them, it takes control of the restraints upon every admission of the life. Then the admissions that had formerly been opened to cravings—admitting delighting appearances, transmitting speech devoted only to worldly entanglements, admitting appropriations that mingle what is unclean with disorder—are no longer used for that reception; and when one stops admitting such things, the inner governing love and thought follow after.

Thus, because the restraints upon the life of the regenerating person are held by enlightened understanding within, that person is opened to admit all that is acceptable to the Divine. The discernment is opened to take in perceptions of genuine love and justice. For this reason, what once appeared attractive—splendid external truths and persuasive appearances fabricated to adorn craving and excite self-love—used to be pleasing to that person’s outward discernment. But now, by the power of enlightened understanding that has filled the person and lived in the outer life, craving that formerly ruled has been humbled. The displays of craving have become repugnant to the regenerating person; but the qualities of the Divine—justice, humility, and the preference for simple truths not fashioned for self-display—are pleasing.

Likewise, the receptivity to instruction had once been open to vain teachings, seductive persuasions, and concealed practices of evil. These were pleasing at the time they were received. But now, by the power of enlightened understanding, seductive persuasions and the deceptive doctrines of evil have become repugnant, and the person is no longer willing to receive them. Instead the person continually delights to receive teachings of justice, the affections of worship, the elevations of prayer, the acknowledgement of the Divine, the instruction of truth, and the understanding of charity.

In sum, all outer admissions were once open to evil, but now have been opened to good. Disorder was ruling in the outward life then, doing whatever it wished, with nothing higher commanding it.

But now authority has been taken away from disorder in the outward faculties. Living good from the Divine has become the ruling power over all operations. It has bound them in stable harmony, and confirmed them in the certainty of truth. It has opened the outer admissions to good; therefore good enters by discernment and by receptivity to instruction, and it dwells in the central governing love. Divine influence reigns and produces what accords with itself. It annuls the rule of disorder as both the initiating impulse and the final purpose; in its place the Divine willing is carried into effect, and the intention of enlightened understanding is fulfilled.

Therefore by wisdom and practiced skill set firm protection around the outer circuit of life’s admissions, so that the disorder that still resides in the outer level has no power over you; so that it does not take away your understanding of truth, nor scatter it into conflicting states, nor drive it from one form to another in ever-changing distortions.

fills.fill: it came up again in them and entered the rulers
fills.notes: The spiritual sense requires a return of the same disordering principle through the malformed works (abortions) back into the governing powers. This supplies the transition into ¶3–¶4 where it ‘assumes’ the fruits and speaks in the chief ruler, and later ‘went into the rulers through the fruits’.

Restores the needed link from ¶2’s return of Matter in the abortions to its presence ‘in the fruits’. The teaching-layer voice is impersonal and sequential: the disorder rises again, then is present ‘in the fruits’.

fills.fill: the form of Adam and Eve after the likeness of the exalted one
fills.notes: The leader’s project in the oldest substrate is the fabrication of a human likeness modeled on the higher pattern; ¶4 explicitly says they ‘formed Adam and Eve after the likeness’. This gap completes the causal statement ‘and he constructed …’.
Matches ¶2 verbatim and keeps the substrate’s structural repetition: the same ‘sin’ as gross Matter bursting from the rulers.
The spiritual sequence requires: lodged in the tree, then rises in the fruits, then takes on their quality (‘assumed them’) before entering and driving the rulers.
Provides the required causal hinge: it enters the rulers and, by its driving efficacy, they produce the human form (Adam and Eve).
Completes the parallelism: it ‘assumed them’ and they ‘too sculpted’ by the same borrowed force; ‘with it’ keeps the impersonal mechanism of influx.
The line describes successive begetting ‘each according to his destiny’; the oldest-layer register prefers impersonal succession of states, here rendered as ‘generations’.
Paragraph 7 anticipates ¶8’s explicit treatment of the eyes. The missing phrase should introduce the specific outward faculty being exemplified.
Fits the correspondential point: the outward organ is for noticing ‘every type’ presented externally; ‘sights’ is the natural carrier for ‘images’ developed in ¶8.
Completes the thought: receiving ‘every type’ and placing it within the internal repositories, which the chapter repeatedly calls storehouses.

fills.fill: every image that it stored within,
fills.notes: After ‘think and seek’ the faculty searches its inner memory for what was deposited; the phrase must point to the retrieved stored image before ‘and it brings it out’.
Balances the triad in the sentence: lustful, loveable, hateful; the spiritual sense lists craving, genuine love, aversion.
The remaining category is aversion. The natural text already ends with ‘hateful’; this gap supplies the generic ‘something’ leading into ‘hateful’.
The ears ‘guard’ what was received; the thing guarded is the deposit in inner repositories, consistently termed storehouses in this chapter.
Required by the repeated mechanism: questioned → goes into inner repositories → searches → brings out. Scent follows the same order as eyes and ears.
Pairs with the next phrase ‘storehouse and remember’: the faculty searches within its storehouse to recall the stored odour.
Specifies the object of recollection in the scent faculty; keeps the chapter’s repetitive, enumerative style.
The mechanism is volitional recall: when asked, if it so chooses, it sends out the remembered taste. This matches the impersonal faculty-language of the chapter.

fills.fill: if they ask it for what was entrusted to it, it brings it out
fills.notes: The steward simile demands the same retrieval formula used throughout: deposit entrusted → stored in distinct vessels → when requested → produced from the place it was set. This also leads smoothly into ¶16 ‘… in the place that it put it.’
Completes ‘hands’ and keeps the parallel list of faculties whose deposits can be produced on request.
Matches the chapter’s fixed pair for inner retention; touch is brought out ‘into’ these internal places before being given outwardly on request.
The analogy requires interior ‘holding rooms’ behind the watchposts and gates, corresponding to inner containments behind the senses.
Completes the enumeration of restraints upon admission points, aligning with the later ‘number of door bolts’.
Supports the phrase ‘there are a mass … them’: a mass ‘within them’ (inside the holding rooms and gates).
‘Door bolts of the gates’ keeps the concrete image and matches the later ‘guards control the bolts of the gates’.
Required by ‘the number … are …’: the teaching stresses multiplicity of restraints and containments.
Leads into the closing clause: when someone wishes ‘to bring out’, he controls the bolts, opens, and brings out the hidden one.

The righteous person’s opened sight receives what corresponds to genuine love and right order; ‘love and righteousness’ is already present, so the gap likely completes ‘love … and righteousness’ as ‘love and justice’ in the older structural register.
Removes the scribal double-l in ‘Holly’ to keep the oldest-layer register consistent while preserving the intended cosmological agent opposed to Sin.

assessment: Most lacunae are trivial letter-restorations and are secure. The substantial gaps occur at ¶2 #8, ¶3 #1, ¶3 #4, ¶4 #5–6, ¶4 #12–13, ¶7 #1–4, ¶8 #4 and ¶15 #2, plus several in ¶21. These were restored by enforcing the chapter’s correspondential mechanics: repeated cycles of influx (Matter or a faculty) entering, being stored in inner ‘storehouses and repositories’, and being retrieved on request; and, in the cosmogonic section, the cyclic return of the same disorder through the products (fruits, abortions) into the rulers to fabricate a human likeness after a higher pattern. Exact wording remains moderately constrained by this structural parallelism, though some phrases (especially ¶21’s camp analogy) could admit alternative but equivalent formulations.
